summary: At step 59, the controlled rehumanization path reaches trap.c:selftouch because the hero has no gloves and still wields a cockatrice corpse. JavaScript currently records that call as unported in polyself.c:newman, so it skips the long corpse-contact message and the following instapetrify path; C pauses on the previous “You feel like a new man!” line before drawing that message, causing the first screen and cursor mismatch. Port whole trap.c:selftouch and wire the selected polyself.c:newman caller.

source.branch: When the primary weapon (or, under the source two-weapon condition, secondary weapon) is a CORPSE whose monster touch_petrifies and the hero lacks Stone_resistance, selftouch prints the caller-supplied phrase plus corpse name, builds the killer phrase, and invokes instapetrify. If stoning is survived, it unwields the corpse when gloves and stone resistance are still absent.
callers: polyself.c:newman:463-465 calls selftouch(no_longer_petrify_resistant) after polyman() and the post-rehumanization refreshes; this is the admitted session path and the only caller wired by this task.
dependencies: trap.c:instapetrify is already implemented in js/trap.js and supports wielding-corpse protection-loss callers; it issues the stoning message and enters done(STONING).
mondata.c:touch_petrifies, do_name.c:obj_pmname, objnam.c:an, and wield.c:uwepgone/uswapwepgone already have JavaScript implementations used by other callers.
artifact.c:retouch_equipment remains an explicit gap in newman and is outside this source scope; the recorded branch reaches selftouch after that call.

evidence: The authoritative saved queue at /home/vtjeng/development/vtjeng/teleport-contest/.cache/latest-saved-combined-queue.json (SHA-256 781129791f95cd10ec8578dd170fd5298182a9b4ad578f5c008d93d68d5bc37b) identifies this admitted v39 session with 5 remaining screens, 64 steps, 59/64 screens and 60/64 cursors matched, and all 2306/2306 RNG calls matched. The first mismatch is segment 0, step 59, newline: C cursor [32,0,1] and “You feel like a new man!--More--”; JavaScript cursor [3,10,1] and no More marker.

Direct JavaScript replay on examined commit 730b2417130fc0c0bf5193cf26ce0028156a7e55 reproduces the boundary: JS step 59 shows “You feel like a new man!” with cursor [3,10,1], then treats each of the four following spaces as an unknown command; C uses those spaces to dismiss the selftouch, instapetrify, and wizard death prompts.

The admitted recording’s actions first use #polyself to become a stone golem, wield a cockatrice corpse, then use #polyself to request human. At polyself.c:463-465, newman calls selftouch(no_longer_petrify_resistant) when !uarmg. The matching JS caller in polyself.js:newman at line 1698 instead records note_unported("trap.c selftouch").

C trap.c:selftouch at lines 3883-3910 checks wielded CORPSE objects with touch_petrifies and !Stone_resistance, prints "%s touch the %s corpse.", builds the killer phrase, calls instapetrify, and after lifesaving calls uwepgone when the hero still lacks gloves/resistance. The source-order message call makes topl.c:update_topl show --More-- on the prior newman message when the longer contact line cannot share it.

The continuation is already owned by existing code: trap.c:instapetrify (js/trap.js:356-375) handles stone-golem transformation or the urgent “You turn to stone...” and done(STONING) path; touch_petrifies, obj_pmname, an, uwepgone, and uswapwepgone are already imported implementations. No RNG call is involved in the first divergence.
